title: PreToolUse hook permissionDecision 'allow' is ignored: rtk-rewritten commands prompt (grep -> rtk grep asks in acceptEdits)
observed: kiln defect (parity). Steps: Andre's settings include PreToolUse hook ~/.claude/hooks/rtk-rewrite.sh, which returns {hookSpecificOutput:{permissionDecision:'allow', updatedInput:{command:'rtk ...'}}}. In acceptEdits on Opus, the model ran 'grep -n ... store.go'; kiln applied updatedInput and then gated 'rtk grep -n "func (r Record) Expired" -A4 store.go', showing 'Allow kiln to run this command?' with option 2 'don't ask again for: rtk grep *'. Same for 'rtk go build ./...' (option 2 offers the broader 'rtk go *'). internal/claude/hooks/runner.go:212 only handles permissionDecision == 'deny'; 'allow' and 'ask' are dropped. With Andre's real config, every rtk-rewritable read command (grep, ls, cat, git status, go build) prompts in kiln but not in Claude Code.
expected: Claude Code (src/services/tools/toolHooks.ts resolveHookPermissionDecision): a hook 'allow' skips the interactive prompt, while deny rules still deny and ask rules still prompt. 'ask' forces a prompt. kiln should do the same, or document the divergence in docs/claude-code-parity.md (it currently lists only rewrite and deny).

fix.note: 2c94b87 and 8642b45 on branch worktree-agent-ae1e528c60b007fe6 (not merged; unit tests only, no real-terminal re-drive with the rtk hook)
